utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom, and up -- out there in The Hague. Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84bis-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for the day, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. And good afternoon in The Hague. Paul Rogers and Aditya Menon appearing for the Prosecution in the remote location; and Ms. Priya Gopalan, Daniela Kravetz, and our Case Manager Line Pedersen in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for Mr. Haradinaj's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Ben Emmerson for Ramush Haradinaj, together with Rod Dixon, Annie O'Reilly, and Andrew Strong in the remote location; and Kerrie Rowan in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Emmerson. And for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning. Gregor Guy-Smith and Colleen Rohan on behalf of Mr. Balaj in the remote location; present in The Hague are Gentian Zyberi and Holly Buchanan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Richard Harvey and Luke Boenisch here together in the remote location; and in The Hague, Mr. Paul Troop and Sylvie Kinabo. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, madam. Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to remind you, and I know you know this already by now, but I must just remind you that you're still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will tell the truth, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to initially start by setting the stage of what was occurring in Kosovo and specifically in your area so that we can have an appreciation of some of the tensions that existed. And if I understand the testimony that you've given thus far, there was, in the month of May, a series of assaults by the Serbian forces against villages in Kosovo, in general, and against your village in specific. True?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the intensity of the attack that you were experiencing, your village had been shelled repeatedly. True?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time of the attacks on my village, yes. I mean the two days of the attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. Now, the reality of the situation was, at that time when your village was being attacked, that you had, as a village, very few weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have some weapons that had been bought before, before the war started.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Again, very few.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had some weapons that we had bought with our own money before the war started.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. My question is the number of weapons. You didn't have enough weapons to arm all of the able-bodied fighting men in your village, did you?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The Serbs, on the other hand, had soldiers, all armed, all trained, with heavy weapons, including obviously tanks, bombs, grenade launchers. Apart from guns. Correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And they were an organised force, weren't they? And by that I mean the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And your village, on the other hand, you did not enjoy such organisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't have any such organisation. We could -- you could not equate our organisation with the Serb forces. Serbia was a state, a country, with a hundred years of experience. The whole world knows that. We were not equals. We were not equals with that state.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. And thank you -- thank you for that. At that time - and by "at that time" for this part of our discussion, sir, I'm referring to the month of May - you were a member of the LDK; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Not only at that time, but I was a member even ten years earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And after the war you remained a member of the LDK; correct? And by "after the war," I'm referring to 1998.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you personally had regular meetings with a gentleman by the name of Rugova on Fridays, did you not?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not every Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have meetings, but not every Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when I -- I mentioned the name Rugova, obviously from the speed of your answer and the content of your answer, you know who I'm referring to. But for purposes of the record, I realise I may have moved a bit quickly. So could you tell us who Rugova -- the Rugova that you were meeting with was?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the president of the Democratic League of Kosovo before the war. After the war, he was president of Kosovo. And I did have contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear: Is it so that the LDK that you referred to is the Democratic League of Kosovo that the witness is referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You beat me to the punch, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You beat me to the punch.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So if you could answer His Honour's question, I would appreciate it. I'm sure we all would.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Democratic League of Kosovo was lead by Dr. Ibrahim Rugova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We understand that. But the abbreviation LDK refers to the Democratic League of Kosovo, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You had occasion to meet with the Prosecutor, and by that I mean Mr. Rogers, on the 15th of December, 2010, in The Hague, did you not?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And at the time that you met with Mr. Rogers, you were tape-recorded; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know whether they recorded it or not. I can't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I don't know whether it helps: It was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like to take the stand, Mr. Rogers?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Just making an admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It might make things go quicker. I'm trying to decide which bundle to use, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could refer to the bundle that's in front of you, sir, and specifically refer to 03075. If you could open to that document. And I would like --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be tab number 6 in your binders, Your Honour. And I'm going to refer -- yes. Tab number 6. And I would refer the Court and counsel to page 7, the bottom of the page, the last four lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to go to page 7. Again, the last four lines. My first question is for you to tell us when you've had an opportunity to read -- to finish reading those lines, that you indicate that you have.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On the 15th of December, 2010, you were asked the following question, and you gave the following answers to Mr. Rogers; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "Mr. Rogers: Go on --"

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: In fact, it's not my initials, it's Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: It's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your response: "And I was in meetings every Friday with the leader Ibrahim Rugova." That's what you said; right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said it was not on every Friday. What I meant was that I met him on Fridays but I also met him on other days. But the main meetings were on Fridays.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. So you met him more than every Friday?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm a bit concerned about your qualification of "maybe." If you have met him every Friday, as you've indicated in your answer to the Prosecution, and you indicate that met him more than every Friday, or on other days, then you met him on more occasions; correct? So there wouldn't be a "maybe" there. That would be a definite yes.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I gave my answer to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I've asked you another question, sir, and I would appreciate an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think, in respect, the witness has answered the question. The passage was put to him, he agreed that that is what it says and what appears to have been said during the course of the interview. He then went on to give an explanation about that. Where he elicited further information. And Mr. Guy-Smith is pursuing him now into the frequency of meetings. I think Your Honours have a sufficient understanding of the frequency of meetings. It's not necessary to continue to pursue this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Whether or not Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Whether or not Mr. Rogers believes this to be a good place or not, that the pursuit of the frequency of meetings is quite distinct from the issue of whether or not the witness answers questions or not. And I'm looking for an answer to a question. I believe unless the question forms -- as formed has a legal objection as a basis, the question should be answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, will you answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. The meetings were very frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And those meetings occurred where, sir?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were held in Prishtina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to turn our attention to another matter now, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: (redacted), I'm going -- oh, excuse me. Because of the sensitivity of the witness's stated concerns, and we need a redaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, ma'am. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, thank you so much. Mr. Registrar, if you could do me the kindness of giving this bundle to the witness. I previously showed this to Mr. Rogers in an attempt to expedite.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could -- you're moving a little too quickly there. Sir, you're moving a bit quickly. If you could concern yourself with tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that would be tab 5 for you as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You're at the wrong tab, sir. 5. You had occasion (redacted), to meet with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, did you not?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. You had occasion to meet with a gentleman by the name of Ole Lehtinen and another individual by the name of Philippe Valleries-Roland?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At that time -- if could you go to paragraph 17, please. Right before you read that -- Witness, right before you read that, you've rendered a number of opinions in this courtroom during these proceedings. You've given us your opinion about a number of things; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the things that happened, I told you about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And -- as -- as I understand, you take full responsibility for your words and your opinions; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can also document the things that I've said here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. You told the two individuals that we just mentioned that, and I quote: (redacted) (redacted). And then you go on: "I would be surprised if he ever had the courage to be a witness in The Hague for what he endured during the war, but if he did, I think he would be a good witness." That's what you told him; right? COUNSEL FOR WITNESS: I apologise, the copy before this gentleman is in English, not in his native Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, okay, I'll give him a copy in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's just behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It should be just behind it. But right before we get to that, okay, and I do appreciate, of course, that he has a right to information in whatever language he prefers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You speak English, do you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you read English?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your honours, that's two things. One is the name -- can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please. May we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Guy-Smith, before you proceed, can you provide the people in The Hague --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- with correct identification of the documents so that they can pull them up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, that document number would be 1D15-0094.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'll -- since I did, in fact, err, let me ask the question again. You stated that: "I would be surprised if he," referring to your travelling companion, "ever had the courage to be a witness in The Hague for what he endured during the war, but if he did, I think he would be a good witness." That's what you said; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. If he told the truth, yes. To my recollection, he hasn't spoken the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Have you been following these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't follow the proceeding, but I heard from some people close to me, a relative -- relatives of mine -- If it's possible, I would like to move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, ma'am. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I will be referring now to information that's contained in tab 49. We will be spending some time there, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, document number for The Hague, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The document number for the The Hague would be 1D15-0332. That's where the document begins. And I thank you for the reminder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your travelling companion was, as -- as you have told us you were, a member of the LDK; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And he was the LDK representative for a number of villages; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only -- he was responsible only for our village. His brother covered several villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your village, the KLA established a presence sometime in the month of April. April/May. Correct? Of 1998. I'm referring now to 1998.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in your village there are a number of members of the KLA who lived in your village, such as --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And now I'm not sure if we should go into private session or not. So rather than be -- upset Mr. Rogers or anyone else, may we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I think it's fair to say that around the (redacted) the Serb forces launched an attack on your village; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- let me put the question to you a different way, then. Around the (redacted), apart from what you said, an attack was launched on your village; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: While that attack was being launched, the women and children of the village were evacuated. Makes sense. Responsible thing to do.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We withdrew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what was left in the village were about 60 men defending your village; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately. I don't know exact number, but there were some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, does the number 60 seem, to you, to be about the right number? Maybe a couple fewer, maybe a couple more, but roughly the right number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: He said approximately, which would appear to be a rough number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Is that an objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes, because it's asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: You're asking him to speculate on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take your -- I take your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the evening, you left your village with your travelling companion; correct? And others, admittedly. But you were with your travelling companion.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And a number of -- of villagers - and those are, from what I understand from your testimony, the men who had been attempting to defend your village - travelled together up to the area of (redacted); right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some stayed in (redacted). Some went on towards (redacted), passing through the (redacted). Not all of them stayed in (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the ones that went on towards (redacted) included yourself and your travelling companion; right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you made a suggestion, because you knew somebody, about what an ultimate good location would be. And you suggested to your travelling companion that you should go to a particular village; right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you arrived at that village late in the evening; right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just for the record, can I kindly ask counsel to turn off his microphone while witness is answering questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You arrived in that village late that evening; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before we arrived at the village, at the (redacted) we met some people whose names I have constantly referred to you during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is my understanding that it's your position that the village, comment of the village, should be in private session? Okay. Could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, can we please ask for a minute. The court reporter here seems to have a technical difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just hold it, Mr. Witness. We've got a problem out there. And while that problem is being attended to, may I say, Mr. Guy-Smith, when you say "we'll get to that, we'll get to that" in that aggressive manner, because already the -- interpreted talking, poor lady, and let her finish. And once she has finished, then you can say we will get to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: She couldn't stop. She had to finish what she had heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Unfortunately I don't have the freedom to be listening in both languages. And those of you who are in the booth, accept my heartfelt apologies. If I'm speaking too quickly or I'm speaking too loudly, please let me know. I'm more than happy to be scolded.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have technical problems with transcript, so we should stop speaking. If you wish this part to be a part of public record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Should we take the break now so that we ... okay. Then we won't.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, can the witness say "testing" or "1, 2, 3" so that we can just try it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you just say "test, test, test," into your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Test, test, test.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Test, test, test.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we be heard? Can he -- is the witness being heard out there in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, just a second. We hear the witness, but the interpreter is to low, so ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I can hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but what is too low?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] The interpretation of the witness does not get clearly through to the court reporter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can hear you, Madam Interpreter, but I don't know whether Madam Registrar out there can hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We also hear the Registrar in The Hague twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh. Must be a bit of a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, can we once again test the witness, if he can say -- [Microphone not activated] ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Test, test, test. Can you hear me? Test.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Test, test, test.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Test, test, test.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you hear that, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, I can. But the court reporter still seems to have the same problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if we might revisit the suggestion of rising at this stage. I only say that because, of course, we're sitting an hour early. We've taken the first hour, which is our extra hour, and I think if we were to take a break now, we would then fall into line with the one-and-a-quarter-hour slots that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was going to -- I was thinking of that, too. Madam Registrar, do you need a break to be able to attend to this problem?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, I'm advised by the technician that we don't need a break. But we need to adjust the volume or the system, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And who does that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] There is a technician attending the court reporter in the courtroom, Your Honour. Okay, Your Honours, can we try once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you say again "test, test, test."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Test, test, test.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Test, test, test.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, that seems to be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that okay? Okay. We'll then carry on. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, could you admonish the witness that when a question isn't before him, he really shouldn't be reading the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Witness, yes, you have been given documents before you, but don't read them unless and only when you are referred to them. Okay? Just concentrate on answering the questions of the lawyer. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We're good?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you still want to stay in private session, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I'd like to go into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, for the record, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You had mentioned while we were in private session that you had gone to (redacted); correct? On your way to the village that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in (redacted) you were with your travelling companion; correct? I'm sorry -- yes, you were with your travelling companion; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Referring Court and counsel to page 7422, lines 12 through 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your travelling companion was asked the following questions, gave the following responses, concerning the interaction that you have discussed previously in your testimony here. I'd like you to hear what he had to say, and then I have some questions to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to stop there for just a moment and revisit some of the discussion that we had at the outset of this session in which you told us that there were not a sufficient number of weapons for the defence of your village. And my question to is that this was a general problem, was it not, at the time, a sufficient number of weapons in order to defend or repel the Serb advances?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. This was the second time we were stopped at Jabllanice --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if you would keep my question in mind. Because my question deals with the adequacy of weaponry that you had.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier that we could not measure up with the enemy. We -- there were not enough weapons to go around.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Before the next question is put, can we just go into private session, please. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We'll take a break and come back at ten to 10.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. An "oda" is a particular room in many Kosovar Albanian homes, is it not?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can you tell us what an "oda" is?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The "oda" is a room used by men. Males.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's a room used by men to drink coffee, rakija, sing songs, and discuss matters of importance; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you talking the position, then, that those statements made by your travelling companion are not true?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of my proximity in terms of relationship with him, I can't say that these are lies. But I'm telling you that he has not described the reality as it was, as it really was. Some things need to be cleared up. But that's his business, whether he wanted to speak the truth or not. That's none of my business. He will be held responsible for not -- if not speaking the truth. I am telling you what I know, what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have told us about an incident that you claim occurred in which a young man's ear was cut off; right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned it several times. And I am here to testify -- I can testify about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You told us that -- you told us that when the ear -- I'm sorry. You told the Prosecutor, in a previous statement that you made --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Referring Court and counsel to tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which would be, for purposes of your situation, 03046.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's tab 1 for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if you could go to paragraph 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, should we be in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why? We may have to -- something may come that will have to be in private session. I thought you wanted it all in private. Do I detect an attempted advantage here of some sort?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... no. No, no, no, we --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If he wishes to go in open session, I'll go into open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: We've moved away from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: -- the contentious areas --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let's go into open --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: -- the village in the statements. That's the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then I'm happy to be in open session. I always prefer open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I was surprised you were so resistant all of a sudden.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was trying to accommodate Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You said the following concerning what you claim you saw: "When the ear fell down on the ground, it was vibrating in the dust, as a butterfly when you drop it in the dust and it tries to get out from it." Right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. That was what I experienced. I don't know how other people viewed it or experienced it. But, for me, it was horrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. You had an opportunity to view a number of photographs, did you not? And that's the photographs with regard to potential alleged victims in this case. Do you remember doing that?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see those photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you the question, then, as follows: Do you recall on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Referring Court and counsel to tab 11, which is 1D15-1519. And I'm referring to paragraph number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall, on the (redacted), meeting with an investigator by the name of Lorenzo Quiroz, also present was Mr. Lehtinen, and at that time you were shown a number of photographs?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. If they showed me any photographs, they were not photographs of victims, but other photographs. I can't say what photographs they were. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's an indication that there was a note that you were shown several photographs. You were shown a photograph of --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I seem to have a problem with the tab numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Tab 11?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes. Tab 11 gives me something else that my colleague has.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: May I approach?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may approach the Bench, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's an indication that you'd been shown several photographs. You were shown a photograph of Ivan Zaric. After examining it closely, you state confidently that you have seen the man and the face is familiar, but cannot specify where you have seen him.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I viewed a lot of photographs, and I can't remember what sort of photographs I was shown. I signed the photographs that I viewed. But they were photographs of victims and of people who are alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were also shown a photograph of an individual by the name of Nasret Alija, and you were unable to recognise him. And you indicate that you think it might be an gentleman by the name of Qamil Behramaj; right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you can't remember, does that mean you're having a failure of recollection, or you're denying that it occurred?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not denying that it occurred. It happened. And I'm saying here that those things happened. If they are alive or dead, somebody must have a look at it and check whether it -- what I'm saying is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I now want to return to your travelling companion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could go back to tab number 50. And I'm going to start at page 7471. This is just to focus us in terms of time. Question, at the bottom of 7471, lines 22 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, this, again, is testimony in private session. Should we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, I thought we were. You're right. Yes. Back into private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was your travelling companion with you; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At the time the ear of the young man was being cut.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Please. Mr. Emmerson will have his turn in asking me questions, and I will give him answers to his questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. The Chamber is looking after that. Don't -- just answer Mr. -- the lawyer's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You put to the witness the part you submit he agrees with and the part you submit he doesn't agree with.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The part you agree that -- the part that you agree to is that he did not see a young boy having his ear cut off. And the part that you disagree with -- correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Can you repeat it again, please. Do you mean me or my travelling companion?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your travelling companion.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, what is this about? Could you explain it again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. You -- you agree that your travelling companion did not see the young boy 's ear cut off, correct? As you claim it happened.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He also doesn't accept that they were taken

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you don't agree with his assertion that he saw any rough or ill-treatment of people while he was at the Jabllanice headquarters; right? Because you said, among other things, (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that Mr. -- I think Mr. Emmerson may well be mistaken in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed, then, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you explain what you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. When you were in Jabllanice with your travelling companion, neither of you were beaten; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. (redacted) was beaten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want to discuss with you what you saw with regard to Skender Kuqi. Now, you've given us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Do we need to stay in private session? I don't mind. I'm just asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was put to you, sir. You're the one on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't believe that we do, but I'm waiting at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, I'd like to see if I understand generally your position concerning Skender Kuqi's physical condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we go to tab 4. That would be in that smaller document there. That's going to be 1D15-0084.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this concerns an interview that you had in Pristina with Mr. Tucker (redacted). COUNSEL FOR WITNESS: I apologise for interrupting, just having some difficulty -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Wrong binder. The plastic cover. And I'm referring the Court and counsel to the paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: In relation to paragraph 6, we have to be careful not to name the other individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I wasn't intending to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No, but the witness may. So it's just a case of telling him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned two individuals in that paragraph. And the first individual, that being the individual who was lucky to survive, do not mention by name. You stated: "He was lucky to survive, because Skender Kuqi who escaped with him was shot, recaptured, and killed by his captors."

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not killed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was he shot?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They shot at him, but he was not killed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So your statement with regard to -- with regard to what happened to Skender Kuqi, as it has it here, is, I take it, inaccurate. He escaped, that's true; right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was captured. He was brought there again to the prison. He was not able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, he escaped; right? And he was escaped, he was recaptured; right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was captured, and they shot at him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... doesn't say that they shot at him in this paragraph. It says he was shot. That indicates that a bullet entered some part of his body. Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether a bullet entered into his body. I cannot confirm that. I can only confirm or assert what I saw. I didn't see any bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... when you made the statement (redacted), you were, at that time, relating something that you saw; right? Or that you claim to have seen. That's what you claimed. You claimed he escaped, you claimed he was shot, you claimed he was recaptured. Right? That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say he was shot at with a bullet. I only said that they fired in his direction, but I didn't say that a bullet caught him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could I perhaps ask that the witness read out loud this part of the -- of his statement in Albanian so that we have it interpreted back to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: It would have to be in private session, I think, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's a name -- there's a name there -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed -- or private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Yes, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's only the sentence starting: "He was lucky to survive, because Skender Kuqi who escaped with him was shot ..." In paragraph 6. So, Mr. Witness, could you read that sentence out loud?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 6, you said, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Not the entire number 6. Only the sentence starting with: "He was lucky to survive, because Skender Kuqi, who escaped with him ..." Et cetera. Only that sentence. Until the end. Until: "killed by his cap tors."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Can I just confirm the witness is looking at the Albanian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's what he should do. And here's -- and here's what I'm asking. In Albanian so he can find the sentence, I suppose. And he should read it in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes. No, I know. But I'm hoping he is looking at the Albanian, not looking at the English. Because it won't help Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He can tell us. COUNSEL FOR WITNESS: If I can be of assistance. He is looking at the Albanian version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it about number 6, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... number 6 says -- starting at where the sentence says: "He was lucky to survive ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's in 6. That's part of 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Third line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see it here, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. [Microphone not activated] Sorry, I'm going to say that again because my mike was off. Just read the whole of paragraph 6 then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a person who is called

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted). This is not so, as I see it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm going to ask a question, and I would like you, Madam Interpreter, to confirm. I'm quoting what you told us in English. You said "because Skender Kuqi, who had escaped with him, was killed, recaptured and killed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So he was killed twice. Is that what you're saying, Madam Interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That's what the witness said, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I just want to be sure, is that what you're saying, sir, that when they -- that he was killed, recaptured, and then killed. Is that your testimony? Okay. It's not your testimony. Is that what is written here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... over it again. Just read that part. Skender Kuqi who escaped with him was ... Read that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "... who had escaped with him, is killed, is captured again, and is killed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Killed, captured, and killed. That's what we're hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what is written here, Your Honour. I don't know how it came to be written like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not fighting with you. I'm just surprised that we see this first "killed" that is being referred to is not what we see in the document that is before us. And I'm just trying to give everybody an opportunity to tell us what is the correct position. Either the interpreter out there, or you, or, you know, but what you are saying -- but if that is what is being said or what is written here, so be it. Mr. Guy-Smith, that's it. He was killed, captured, and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I don't want to get into a situation if --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe he was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: But I'm trying to clarify a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing for you to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Rogers. At this point, if -- if Mr. Kuqi is to be likened to Lazarus, then that's as far as we can take it, and I'm satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Then could Mr. Guy-Smith kindly just go to page 4 of the statement and deal with the declaration, because the declaration is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shouldn't you do that in re-examination, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I can. But it might be sensible to not leave the Court with an impression that's not correct. If we deal with the process of this now, without leaving the record in the state that it's in, thinking that there's some issue about what might or might not have been said. The problem is, is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not a problem. Could you go to the fourth page of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fourth ... you want the fourth page or the fourth paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fourth page. Witness acknowledgment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because the fourth page deals with -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At the time that you -- that you signed this witness acknowledgment, what had occurred was that the statement had been read to you from the English language and translated into Albanian; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know whether it was read to me. I know that I wouldn't have said he was killed. I would have corrected it myself had I known.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we go to page 5. And go to paragraph 4 of page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is the interpretation certification. Go to paragraph 3, first of all. It says: "I have orally translated the above statement from the English language to the Albanian language in the presence of X," that would be you "who appeared to have heard and understood my translation of this statement." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It was not read out to me. Or even if it was read out to me, it was wrongly read out. A long time has passed. The translator, too, might have made a mistake. But I didn't say he was killed and again he was killed. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I understand that a long time has passed and you've taken the position the translator may have made a mistake. But now, going to the next paragraph, paragraph 4, it says as follows: That you have acknowledged that the facts and matters set out in his statement, as translated by me, are true to the best of his knowledge and recollection and accordingly signed the statement where indicated. And that's -- that's what occurred; right?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I am repeating: It was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm mindful of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. When is "then"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's going to be 20 past --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Ten past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies. Sleeping on the job. Yeah. Five more minutes to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Five more minutes to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm looking at your colleague and he -- I'm not sure whether or not he has an intervention or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm just wondering whether you are moving onto something else or whether you continue with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm moving on to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... might it not, then, be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's why I said I noted the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... thank you so much. We'll take a break, then, and come back at quarter to. Court adjourned. Really sleeping all the time. May we move into the closed -- into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. We take a break and come back at quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. -- we are left with two hours and 15 minutes for the remainder of our working day. Mr. Guy-Smith, you had undertaken to finish in about two and a half sessions. Can I take it that we're still there and we can divide the remaining time this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We're very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- can we divide the remaining time this way: We -- we go for an hour, and we'll take a 15-minute break at quarter to 1.00, to 1.00, and then take the remaining hour to 2.00. Can -- are you going to finish within a quarter of the first hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How long are you going to take, still?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Over the break, I excluded some more questions from the questions that I already had, because I understand the pressures. I'm going to take at least a half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At least a half an hour. Hopefully ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I pause there for a minute. With regard to the massacre of the family Jashari, could you tell us, if you know, what he's referring to?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. I'm not going to say anything regarding that family. It's got nothing to do with me. Don't -- please don't ask me about such things. It is a sacred family. I cannot say anything about that family.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say it's a sacred family, what you mean by that is that the entire Jashari family was massacred by the Serbian forces in 1998, March of 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I told you sometime ago that I wanted to discuss with you Skender Kuqi and what you have told us you saw. And as I understand your testimony, you saw Skender Kuqi's -- and I hope you can help me here. You saw his guts hanging off of his body, saw his kidney outside of his body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I did not see his intestines, but I saw the body that was cut; and as far as I could see, the kidneys were open.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And at the time that you saw -- so if I understand your testimony, you saw his -- his kidney, was it -- was it hanging outside of his body? Was it on top of his body? What was it then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have five minutes to go, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm fully appreciative of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were inside, but his back was cut up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: For your purposes, it's going to be 0346 [sic]. For our purposes, it's going to be tab 1, and specifically referring to paragraph 29.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the clarity of transcript, Your Honours: It's 03046.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. And I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And referring to the condition of -- of his body, you state the following: "I could also observe that Skender's tongue was hanging out from his mouth and was something I had never seen before. The tongue was hanging so far out from his mouth that it looked like the tongue of a cow. I could also observe that part of his guts were visible on his back. First I thought it was his bowels, but then I understood it had to be a kidney. It was an open wound and the kidney was visible outside his body, a horrible sight." My question to you is: Is that what you claim you saw? That's what happened?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm saying that I saw it. The kidney was not outside the body. The back was cut open. When you say "outside the body," it means that it was detached from the body. It wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Referring the Chamber and counsel to paragraph -- I'm sorry, tab 26, which is 1D15-0521.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is a statement given to Mr. Obruca, by a gentleman whose last name is Shehaj, a doctor who dealt with Mr. Kuqi. Dealing specifically with paragraph number 8, about seven lines down he refers to what happened when Mr. Kuqi was brought to the hospital. "Kuqi was brought inside, and I made the first examinations of his health conditions. I could not see any open wounds and he was in a state of delirium. He was disoriented and not able to communicate. At the first look, he had symptoms of a person who had kidney problems because he had a swollen face, swollen feet, and swollen hands. Later on, it was found that he had a kidney failure and that both kidneys were completely blocked."

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who said this, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Said by Dr. Shehaj, who treated Skender Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He might have spoken here about his real situation, and if he has, one thing he has forgotten, which means that his kidneys were open. You could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Finally on this subject, if we could turn to tab 24. Which is, for purposes of the Registry, 1D15-0519. And I want to talk about this as well as -- and ask you about your responses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before the question comes, I'm not suggesting it's improper to put the question, but what I just want to say - and I'm sure the Court very much has this in mind - these medical documents are not in evidence. And until they are in evidence, the answer from this witness as to his views and/or what he observed will be final. Until such time as they have been admitted, they are not evidence in this case. And Your Honours, I'm sure, will be treating them with due care and caution, because they would need to be called, and the Prosecution -- because they will be called not part of the Prosecution case, the Prosecution would then wish to examine these doctors on the very points, particularly the last doctor. This one is simply expressing an opinion. Of course, this is also expert evidence that would need to have leave to be called. So I'm just asking Your Honours to treat it with a degree of caution at this stage, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Dr. Jerreat states the following: "In paragraph 15 of the first statement there was a description of a young Serb boy having his ear grabbed and ear cut off without any problems in the cutting process. The ear fell down on the ground and was vibrating in the dust as a butterfly when you drop it in the dust and when it tries to get out from the it. "Comment: "This is a physical impossibility. The ear is constructed of skin and largely cartilage. There are also blood vessels and nerves. There are no muscles and there is no capability for independent movement of the ear. Even blood drops falling from the head onto the ear would not be of sufficient force to cause movement of a severed ear." He goes on: "In paragraph 29 there were two descriptions I can comment upon. First [sic] the tongue was said to be hanging so far out from his mouth that it looked like the tongue of a cow. "Comment: "Physically in life by active movement some people may be able to extend the tongue to the lower chin. "Firstly, I would not describe this as the appearance of a cow's tongue which is of an entirely different appearance. And secondly I would not expect a person who was alleged to have ... severe injuries over a swollen body to have the ability to protrude his tongue in such a matter [sic]. "In a later section he described 'I could also observe that parts of his guts was visible on the back. First I thought it was his bowels, but then I understood it had to be a kidney.' "'It was an open wound and the kidney was visible outside of his body, a horrible sight.'" "Comment: "This appearance, which I regard as impossible," and then it goes on. I'll leave that out for the moment. Second paragraph: "The kidneys, as a result of the forward bulge of the lumbar part of the vertebral column (spine) on the posterior (back) abdominal wall, do not lie flat but are tilted at an angle, each effectively hanging down into a 'gutter' at the side of the lumbar vertebrae and the psoas major muscle ... as though suspended by the renal vein and artery. "For a kidney to be seen outside a wound on the body, it would either have to be ripped out from the wound or pushed through the back wound from a force from the front of the kidney. "The results of either of these would be tearing of either renal blood vessels and/or aorta with sufficient" -- I'm sorry, "with subsequent massive blood loss which would be gushing forth --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel slow down, please, for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's request from the interpreters. Mr. Guy-Smith, you heard the request.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can I start again? I'm asking the interpreter. Madam interpreter, may I start again?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll start with "The results ..." "The results of either of these would be tearing of either renal blood vessels and/or aorta with subsequent massive blood loss which would be gushing forth from the alleged body wound. "This type of injury would cause an acute death from blood loss and would not be compatible with swelling of the body from renal failure which occurs over a period of hours, days or even a week dependant upon its cause." Having heard the comments made by Dr. Jerreat, do you maintain the position that you have maintained concerning the ear that flutters like a butterfly, the tongue that hangs like a cow, and the kidney outside of the body?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described to you the situation that I saw myself. I don't know what the doctor -- or how the doctor saw it. I am not a doctor. But I told you what I saw, the condition that he was in, in my eyes. I apologise to his family that I have used this expression "seemed like the tongue of a cow." This is not a nice way of putting it. But that's the impression it gave me when I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have one last short round of questions and then I am done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So you're clear, very clear, about our position: I put it to you that the stories that you've told here about an ear being cut off, about the presence of my client and his involvement in such behaviour, the stories that you've told us about Mr. Kuqi and his condition - none are true. These are things that you did not see, you were not present, you were never detained in Jabllanice, were you? You made it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would like to thank the Court for its --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, if I may interrupt. Mr. -- we believe Mr. Rogers had an intervention a minute ago which did -- that was not recorded, if that can be repeated, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Rogers -- Mr. Rogers just said that was not a fair question, and the question reiterated what he said to Mr. Guy-Smith. And Mr. Guy-Smith rephrased his question. Is that okay? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I thank the Court for its further indulgence in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. Yes, Mr. -- sorry, Mr. Emmerson. Can we take our break and you can start at 1.00? It's going to be about ten and a half minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But I shan't have any questions for the witness, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, you have -- you're turning it over to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not proposing to cross-examine this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Rogers, can we take a short break and we'll start with your -- take a short break, come back at 1.00? Before we go -- I'm so sorry, something is wrong today.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Take a break and come back at 1.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Rogers, you don't -- you're not obliged to take the entire hour. If you leave a couple of minutes for us to do winding up things, that will be very nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't wish to take up the entire hour. I will be as brief as I responsibly can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I have just a few additional questions for you, please. The first relates to evidence you gave in answer to questions by Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: And Your Honours will find it at transcript reference at page T2478. Mr. Witness, you were testifying about the time after you left your village heading in the direction of (redacted) and the whole village, was being put to you, were walking in that direction. You were telling us that (redacted) and how you'd been stopped in (redacted). Just so you understand where I want to ask you. And you said to us -- so, the question came: "So who stopped you at the (redacted)?" And you answered: "(redacted)." In relation to that, when you were stopped in the (redacted), could you tell us, please, what (redacted) said to you when you were stopped?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? I'm not sure I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's all right. I'll withdraw the question and move on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Let me move on, if I may, to the next part. You then told us that you were stopped again in (redacted) and this time - this is at transcript 2479 - this time you mentioned (redacted) (redacted). On that occasion, what, if anything, did (redacted) say to you? Why were you stopped?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I want to deal with another issue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Transcript T2481, for those following the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: And you were being --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: We need to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to move to strike that last answer on the grounds that it was clearly based on hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Hearsay is admissible before this Tribunal. It's a matter of weight at the end of the day. That's his understanding and that's why he says the witnesses -- he uses the phrase that he did. There's nothing to strike out of the record at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: There's no sources provided for this. It is completely insufficient as a statement to provide any -- any kind of credence that this Tribunal can place in it. But, having said that, I'm confident that this Tribunal is perfectly capable of ignoring unsourced hearsay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I just want to clarify, finally, Witness, relating to Skender Kuqi and the matters that were discussed concerning shots. Can you explain, please, what you meant when you referred to shooting concerning Skender Kuqi. What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were gun-shots. When Skender Kuqi tried to escape from prison, in order to stop him, they shot at him. I did not say that -- that the bullet pierced his body or something like that. I said that there were shots at him and he stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... very clear: Was he alive or was he dead?

utterances.speaker: 80 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Skender Kuqi was alive. He was not dead. He was captured alive and was returned to the prison, to the place that I call a prison, and I can draw a sketch of it if you want. I can draw the place where Skender Kuqi was staying and the place where I was staying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I brought the documents that you asked me yesterday -- to bring yesterday. I have a document that proves that I am innocent, that I have not done any evil deeds, and that I behave properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can give them over to Mr. Court Officer. Thank you so much, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are in Albanian. I don't know whether you'll be able to translate them. I was never charged. I have always behaved properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. Mr. Court Officer, if it's possible to make copies and then give the witness his copies back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this -- okay. Let's wait for your documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
