utterances.text: Thank you. May the witness be released?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This brings us to the end of your testimony, Mr. Witness. Sorry, just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness has brought these documents in response to my request. I have not had an opportunity to look at them. I don't expect that further questions will arise, but I would like a moment to be able to glean what I can from them, given that I do not speak Albanian, but I just want to have a moment, before the witness is released, in case any matter of seriousness arises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You would like to give them to Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Witness, I was just saying that -- maybe we go into open session. May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Witness, we've come to the end of your testimony. The Chamber just wants to thank you very much for coming forward to come and testify. We understand that at the beginning of your testimony you did indicate that you were not well, but still you have been able to stay on with us for the last five days. So the Chamber is appreciative of that. You are now excused. You may stand down. And please travel well back home. Before do you that, we're going to have to move into closed session, though. And I know that you are expecting to get your documents back, so copies will be made and they will be given to you. May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I saw you rising, Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I'm pleased to be able to say the Prosecution can close its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could just use the last few minutes to deal with some sequential matters arising from the announcement that Mr. Rogers has just made. First of all, having canvassed the position with each of my friends for the Defence, we thought it might be helpful to give Your Honours an idea in broad terms for scheduling purposes of where things may go from here, both in relation to any 98 bis submissions and in relation to the possible scope of Defence cases. Anything that I say now is for indication purposes only, because there is a possibility, obviously, that things may change. But as matters stand - and I'll be corrected if I put the position inaccurately - none of the three accused intends to call any evidence beyond possibly one short viva voce witness, or maybe two, and possibly some documents admitted under the 92 bis. And so the reason I say that is because if there is to be any Defence evidence, you will appreciate that it's unlikely to take more than a single day of Court sitting time. Neither is it likely to require any extended period for the preparation or filing of Defence opening briefs, because the nature of the evidence is such that it would require nothing more than a short covering letter. That being the case, what I propose is this. First of all, that having given that indication, the Tribunal make an order that the three Defence teams formally confirm their position on the record seven days from today, that is, on Friday, the 27th of April, by close of business, and that the Chamber schedule a Status Conference on either Monday, the 30th of April, or Wednesday, the 2nd of May. I'm afraid that I have to be at my mother's funeral on Tuesday, the 1st of May. So since it would be, I think, desirable to have a Status Conference as urgently as possible to clarify the position and set the schedule for the future, may we request either of those two dates. And if neither are convenient, maybe we could get diaries out now and work backwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do you say the 30th of April, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Isn't that an official holiday?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Ah. Shall we say Wednesday, the 2nd of May? So then the Tribunal will have our submission formally in writing by the Friday before; therefore, three days before the Status Conference everybody will know where they stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just on a sideline, our condolences for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When did it happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before we left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So just to recap: Friday the 27th of April for formal filing of the Defence position on 98 bis and a Defence case; a scheduling Status Conference for Wednesday, the 2nd of May, at which dates can be fixed for the submission of any Defence opening briefs, as well as the calling of the limited amount of viva voce evidence that there may be, which one would hope would be able to be called at the first available date; followed by scheduling for closing briefs. So all of that could be dealt with at the Status Conference once we've had a week of intervening in order to ensure that the Defence position can be formalised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Unfortunately, I didn't write the dates as you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was saying Friday, the 27th of April, so that's seven days from today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- at the close of bliss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the submission by the Defence formally of their positions on 98 bis and Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Followed by a Status Conference on Wednesday, the 2nd of May, at which Scheduling Orders can be given. And the plea that, after the 2nd of May, if there is to be viva voce evidence, it be at the first available sitting date at which the witnesses are capable of attending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that's the suggestion. I've got one or two other matters to raise procedurally, but I don't know if Mr. Rogers wants to comment on the suggestion that I've made already or whether he wishes to qualify or add to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, that seems perfectly reasonable. I think the date is [indiscernible] but it can be accommodated by the Court, if that is a sensible date. I do have one issue that I wish to raise myself relating to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you raise it, can we just get confirmation from the other two counsel on the suggestion made by Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I conferred with Mr. Emmerson prior to this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: As did I, Your Honour. We are in agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Rogers, you may --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... I think we've got a shopping list which is going to deal with the issue that Mr. Rogers intends to raise. The next matter so far as Mr. Haradinaj is concerned is that whilst I've been on my feet an application for provisional release has been filed on his behalf. The Prosecution were notified of the application on Wednesday with a view to taking instructions from Prosecutor as to whether or not it could be dealt with by way of oral submissions this afternoon. The position it can't be and therefore an application has been filed in writing. In order to lay the foundation for the application I'm just about to make, which is as to timing for responses in determination, can I please ask the Registry to hand to Mr. Rogers and to Your Honours, not for reading now but for taking away, the application for provisional release, because, of course, it's a Friday evening, very late in The Hague, and I would want the matter to be progressed as speedily as possible. And given that the Prosecutor and Mr. Rogers have been on notice for it for some days, it's right that they should have the opportunity to look at the detail of it. Because I'm going to ask the Trial Chamber to abridge the time for the Prosecutor's written response until 5.00 p.m. on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rogers, you had an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No, I can't do it by 5.00 p.m. on Monday. Your Honours, we will deal with it, I would suggest, by the end of the next week. I need to discuss the matters with the Prosecutor and go through it. And that's the time-frame in which we can do it. To put us in the position of trying to deal with this by distance today would be quite wrong, and we are entitled on normal circumstances to 14 days to respond to these matters. But I am prepared to undertake that we will file a response by the end of next week, by next Friday, which would be seven days shorter than that which we are entitled to under the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You had a issue to raise. Have we covered it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Emmerson can deal with it, because we talked about it earlier, although if he's going to refer to the order, we'll have to go, I'm afraid, into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it's better if that part of the agenda is dealt with in private session in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position is simply this. That because of the way in which this witness's evidence has progressed, obviously there have been the occasional slip in public session, as well as the need to release into public session certain matters that were, out of abundance of caution, took place in private session, subject to redactions. And given the fact that there are more than the usual number of problems associated with that in relation to this witness, the suggestion that we have discussed between the parties is that the Prosecution should file, I think, within seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... we can tie it up with the same time -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly. Within seven days. It's proposals for redaction and the release into public session of any closed or private session material that doesn't need to remain in closed or private session. The Defence, then, to consider and respond. But, as a result, for the Chamber to make an order suspending the automatic release for the public session material in five days until further order. To --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you're just asking us to do that, and which we can do right now, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. It's so ordered that the evidence that has been taken in the remote location shall not be released until further order -- made public until further order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally this. And it may seem -- it may seem like a rather curmudgeonly request. But you -- the Bench has been provided, purely for convenience purposes to available my learned friends to cross-examine so that everyone is working from the same schedule, with a bundle of material which was prepared by the Haradinaj Defence at the time when it was thought that there was a likelihood or a possibility that I would be cross-examining this witness. Now, none of that material has been tendered. And not only that, the file contains material that hasn't even been referred to. And in order that everybody can see that justice is being done according to the way in which it ought to be done, and if that can be not only done but seen to be done, we would request that the material that Your Honours have been given - and that is all of the documentary material that you've been given that has not been exhibited - now be returned to the parties so that nobody can be left under any misapprehension that the Trial Chamber would be doing research of its own. And I know you wouldn't be, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I thought you might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just didn't want to -- some Judges would think that disrespectful, but I know that none of this Chamber would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was just concerned what am I going to do with it, from a weight point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we were hoping --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want yours?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: We were hoping you would take ours back because we understand you have a larger weight limit than we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That only leaves outstanding the documents produced by the witness, and I have nothing to say about that. I don't understand any party yet to have tendered them. They haven't been translated. Can that simply be left in abeyance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you done? Thank you so much. I think -- Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, not to try the patience of all of us who are anxious to leave this beautiful remote location, may I just say there are a couple of housekeeping matters in relation to documents that I tendered that I had provided to the witness yesterday which I did not tender for admission. I will provide a list to the Prosecution, and hopefully we can resolve any outstanding matters in relation to that in the course of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is there to resolve? Do you want to tender them later?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, I -- I can tender -- I can tender them now by listing the exhibit numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: But failing that, then I would wish the opportunity to pursue that with the Prosecution before matters are closed completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Prosecution will indicate to you whether it intends to give you that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber won't be party to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And finally may I say that it is also my intention of Mr. -- on behalf of Mr. Brahimaj to file an application for provisional release. The Court will have that on Monday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: intrusion into their ordinary and regular functions, and I think, if I may say so on behalf of all of the parties and their representatives, we would like to express our thanks for the courtesy and hospitality that's been shown to us throughout this rather difficult week.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I say, on behalf of the Prosecutor, that we do thoroughly endorse every remark that Mr. Emmerson has made. We are extremely grateful for all of the assistance we have received from everybody that has taken part in these proceedings. Not least of all to our own staff from the ICTY who, if I may say, have done an extraordinary job, both here and in The Hague. To make this work is quite astonishing, and a real tribute should be paid to everybody that has taken part in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... and Mr. Rogers for making those thanks to our hosts here, because that's what I've been hoping I would -- the Bench would be able to do in the remaining minutes that we still have. The -- the Chamber endorses every word of what you've said. There's no need to repeat that. Save to add that we are also grateful to you, Mr. Interpreter. We know that you have taken time off your very busy schedule to come and be with us and be available, and we recognise that and we appreciate that, and we are very grateful to you for that.
